newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends higher as hurricane nears U.S.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends higher as hurricane nears U.S.

text.p: CME lumber futures closed higher, but down from early contract highs, in reaction to Hurricane Fran nearing the North Carolina coast, analysts said.

Lumber demand to rebuild after the hurricane should boost cash lumber prices, which already were trending higher, analysts said. Low retail inventories have forced dealers to pay higher prices quoted by saw mills. Strong demand by home builders has kept lumber flowing through marketing channels, analysts said.
Cash spruce prices continued to rise and some analysts reported Thursday's prices ranged from $425 to $430 per tbf, up from $419 quoted Wednesday by Random Lengths.

CME lumber closed up $5.70 to $9.00 per tbf with November up $8.60 at $396.90. November earlier set a contract high of $402.20. The soon-to-expire September was up $5.70 at $435.00, but had peaked early at a contract high of $437.10.
